moduleTitle: Section 8 - API Theory & Create API TestCases
learningObjectives: Convert an API TestCase into a functioning Template.
Link values from the TestSheet to the API Template.
Instantiate the API Template and run the TemplateInstances.
Build a concrete API TestCase (Verify Product by SKU) using Common Parameters and the correct Insert/Verify ActionModes.

elements.text: API Scan can create messages and export selected objects into Commander Modules and TestCases. Inspect the resulting request/response model, endpoint, authentication and assertions before execution. No developer-provided subset was available for this review; local country/product examples are hypothetical, not verified current Demo Web Shop functionality.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Communication Pattern Depends on the Transport

elements.text: For the synchronous web-service example, model a request and verify the corresponding response. This is not a universal rule that every API interaction must consist of exactly two steps; queue push/pull and other transports have different message workflows. Check the transport and expected communication pattern.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Building the API Template (Same Flow as UI)

elements.text: The common Template workflow still applies: prepare the flow, convert, link the data source, inspect XL paths, set generation conditions as required, check and instantiate. API-specific endpoint, authentication, payload, transport and assertion behavior still need separate review. Schema validation and generation do not prove the response meets the business contract.

Independent product example: send a synthetic SKU through an authorized test endpoint and compare returned product fields with agreed expected data. Request payload values use Insert in the documented simple example; response fields being asserted use Verify. Structural selection, buffering or other purposes may require other ActionModes. CP recalls a scoped Test Configuration Parameter, potentially inherited or overridden, rather than a guaranteed project-wide value. Do not assume product ID 36 or catalogue visibility from an inaccessible original exercise.

Convert the prepared API flow to a Template and map synthetic inputs and expected outputs. Deliberately replace an old Value only if that mapping is intended; composed expressions can be legitimate. Inspect unwanted leftover text alongside an XL path without deleting intentional prefixes. Generate, review and trial-run the concrete cases against the agreed contract.

Original Academy exercise instructions, API subset, endpoint contract and solution material were inaccessible and remain unverified. Use the independent example with authorized non-production access; no original API exercise was executed during this review.

examPitfalls.title: Transport matters
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Treating every API as a mandatory synchronous pair.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use the actual protocol and transport model.

examPitfalls.title: Common generation is not complete API validation
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming schema checking proves endpoint and authentication correctness.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Review the API contract and run purposeful response assertions.

examPitfalls.title: CP is scoped
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Treating every configuration value as project-wide.

examPitfalls.title: Composed values can be deliberate
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Deleting all literal text next to an XL expression.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which supported workflow can generate API TestCases and Modules in Commander?

options.text: By manually typing every TestStep from scratch.
By scanning the application's API with Tosca's API Scan feature, collecting Request/Response pairs, and exporting the result.
By importing a Swagger file directly with no further steps needed.
By recording a UI session and converting it automatically.

practiceQuiz.hint: The developers had already done this preparation step.
practiceQuiz.rationale: API Scan exports selected messages into Commander models; the export still needs purposeful configuration and verification.

optionExplanations.A: Manual modelling is possible, but this option does not identify the supported scan/export workflow.
optionExplanations.B: API Scan exports messages as Commander models for later configuration and testing.
optionExplanations.C: Importing a definition does not eliminate configuration and assertion review.
optionExplanations.D: A UI recording does not automatically define the API contract.

practiceQuiz.scenario: For this synchronous request/response web-service example, which structure supports sending input and checking the reply?

options.text: API TestCases can only be run manually, never via ExecutionLists.
API TestCases cannot be converted into Templates.
API TestCases don't use TestSheets or Conditions.
A request step followed by the appropriate response assertions; other transports may use different workflows.

practiceQuiz.hint: Think of the restaurant analogy — an order and its response.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The synchronous example models input and its reply; it is not a universal exactly-two-steps rule for every API.

optionExplanations.A: API TestCases can be arranged for automated execution.
optionExplanations.B: API flows can use Template generation.
optionExplanations.C: Source mapping and generation conditions are supported.
optionExplanations.D: This synchronous scenario has a request and response assertion flow, with transport-specific caveats.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Once an API TestCase's TestSteps are cleaned up and renamed, how does the rest of the Template-building process compare to UI TestCases?

options.text: API Templates require a completely separate Instantiate command.
API Templates skip the Check Template step entirely.
Use the common Template linking, mapping, checking and generation workflow, while also reviewing API-specific transport and assertions.
API Templates cannot use Conditions.

practiceQuiz.hint: The mechanics are the same; only the TestStep type (Request/Response) differs.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The model-generation mechanism is shared, but API payload and transport behavior must still be verified.

optionExplanations.A: The common TemplateInstance operation supplies generation.
optionExplanations.B: Check Template still helps validate the model.
optionExplanations.C: Common generation mechanics coexist with API-specific review.
optionExplanations.D: Generation conditions are not prohibited for API flow models.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Where should you verify current API Scan export and steering behavior for your Tosca version?

options.text: Only a remembered UI-course example.
Only a TestSheet filename.
The current official API Scan and API Engine documentation.
There is no documentation for API testing.

practiceQuiz.hint: Use the primary documentation matching the installed version.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Current vendor documentation describes the version’s export and steering procedures; an inaccessible course label alone does not verify them.

optionExplanations.A: An old UI example does not verify current API export behavior.
optionExplanations.B: A filename is not procedural documentation.
optionExplanations.C: Version-matched primary documentation provides the current procedures.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What does {CP[Email]} recall in an independent API TestStep?

options.text: The available scoped Test Configuration Parameter named Email, including applicable inheritance or overrides.
A link to an Instance on a linked TestSheet.
A buffered value from an earlier TestStep.
An invalid syntax that Tosca will reject.

practiceQuiz.hint: Notice this value is used in Exercise 8a, before any TestSheet is linked.
practiceQuiz.rationale: CP recalls configuration, XL supplies linked source data and B recalls a buffer; scope and overrides matter.

optionExplanations.A: CP recalls the available named TCP with its applicable scope.
optionExplanations.B: Linked source data uses XL rather than CP.
optionExplanations.C: Buffer recall uses B rather than CP.
optionExplanations.D: The shown CP syntax is supported.

practiceQuiz.scenario: You want to assert returned Id and Name fields against independent expected data. Which ActionMode expresses that purpose?

options.text: Insert
Verify
Buffer
WaitOn

practiceQuiz.hint: You're checking what came back, not sending data.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Verify asserts returned values; a buffer captures data without itself proving it matches the expectation.

optionExplanations.A: Insert changes message data rather than asserting the returned expectation.
optionExplanations.B: Verify compares returned fields with expected values.
optionExplanations.C: Buffer captures data but does not itself assert the expected match.
optionExplanations.D: WaitOn synchronization is not the stated immediate comparison purpose.

practiceQuiz.scenario: You intend to replace an old static Value entirely with a new XL mapping. Which controlled preparation fits?

options.text: Replace the old Value deliberately and inspect the resulting XL expression.
Set the WorkState to COMPLETED first.
Resolve every Reference in the TestCase.
Nothing — Tosca automatically replaces old values with new XL references.

practiceQuiz.hint: This is the same rule that applies everywhere else in this course.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Intentional replacement differs from composing a value; do not rely on an automatic drag operation to guarantee the desired mapping.

optionExplanations.A: A deliberate replacement and inspection addresses the intended mapping.
optionExplanations.B: Completed does not establish this expression mapping.
optionExplanations.C: Every shared reference need not be resolved.
optionExplanations.D: Automatic replacement is not a semantic correctness guarantee.

practiceQuiz.scenario: After mapping an XL expression, what should you inspect in its Value field?

options.text: Check the full expression and remove only unwanted leftover text, retaining intentional composition.
Whether the Module was renamed to "GetProductBySku Response".
Whether the ExecutionList folder exists.
Nothing further is needed once the XL reference is visible.

practiceQuiz.hint: Linking can leave a stray value behind if the field wasn't fully cleared.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Literal prefixes can be intentional. Inspect the whole expression rather than deleting everything except the XL path.

optionExplanations.A: Inspect intentional composition and remove only unwanted leftover text.
optionExplanations.B: Module naming alone does not validate the composed Value.
optionExplanations.C: ExecutionList presence does not validate this path.
optionExplanations.D: A visible XL reference alone does not establish a correct full expression.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which description characterizes the networked web-service example used here?

options.text: They include both network dependent and independent APIs
A service interface accessed through network communication, unlike a purely local in-process API.
APIs that do not require a network to operate
Tosca functionalities that allow us to test websites

practiceQuiz.hint: It's the narrower of the two API categories — the one that needs a connection.
practiceQuiz.rationale: This example involves service communication; not every API requires a network, and a network need not mean the public Internet.

optionExplanations.A: This improperly includes purely local interfaces in the networked example.
optionExplanations.B: The service is accessed through network communication.
optionExplanations.C: A purely local interface is outside this stated networked example.
optionExplanations.D: Web services are application interfaces, not a Tosca website-testing command.

options.text: Application Processing Intelligence
Application Programming Input
Application Programming Interface
Application Processing Information

practiceQuiz.hint: The last word describes what connects two applications — a boundary they talk across.
practiceQuiz.rationale: API stands for Application Programming Interface — a set of rules that lets applications communicate with each other, with or without a network (web services being the network-dependent subset).

optionExplanations.A: Processing Intelligence is not the expansion of API.
optionExplanations.B: Programming Input substitutes an incorrect final word.
optionExplanations.C: API expands to Application Programming Interface.
optionExplanations.D: Processing Information is not the expansion.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is one useful reason to test an API directly?

options.text: To assert behavior exposed through a service interface, including functions not exposed in the UI.
So we can read the code
API testing does not require Internet connection
We don't need to do API testing as everything can be accessed through the UI

practiceQuiz.hint: A UI is not required for a callable service function.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Direct API testing can verify a service contract even where no UI exposes the function; it does not imply every function lacks a UI.

optionExplanations.A: Direct interface assertions can cover behavior unavailable through a UI.
optionExplanations.B: Testing behavior does not require source-code access.
optionExplanations.C: Network connectivity depends on the target, so this is not a universal reason.
optionExplanations.D: UI access is not guaranteed to cover the complete service contract.

quickRecap.value: API Scan exports selected messages into models that still need inspection.
Model the actual protocol; synchronous request/reply is not every API interaction.
Use common Template mechanics, then verify the actual API contract.
CP values can be inherited and overridden; XL and B serve distinct purposes.
Inspect complete expressions; keep deliberate prefixes and remove unwanted leftovers.
